newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CPI proves cue for Australian bond profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: CPI proves cue for Australian bond profit-taking.

text.p: *Australian bonds succumbed to profit-taking as the March quarter inflation report failed to live up to the extremely optimistic outcome that had been built in over recent days.
*Scope for policy easing still seen by some analysts.

"However, much will depend on the next few sets of activity statistics -- retail trade, building approvals, and, particularly, employment," he added, putting the chance of a rate cut at 30 percent in the next few months.
March quarter CPI was just a tad above median expectations at up 0.2 percent on the quarter, but this still saw the headline rate at 1.3 percent and its lowest in four years.
Underlying inflation was in line with expectations at up 0.4 percent for an annual rate of 2.1 percent, remaining at the bottom end of the Reserve Bank's 2.0-3.0 percent target.

The data follows Tuesday's moderate A$10 per week low pay award granted by the Australian Industrial Relations Commission and further removed the risk of the Reserve Bank tightening monetary policy this year.

Indeed, there is a small group of analysts that believe, like Colonial's Kunnen, the RBA now has scope to ease policy again if it feels that the economy needs a further stimulus and some are even looking to the May board meeting for such a move.
However, "We remain of the view that interest rates are likely to have bottomed for this cycle," said Su-Lin Ong, fixed income economist at Hambros Bank.
"(But) Should forthcoming leading indicators of activity deteriorate sharply, then the chances, albeit slim, of another rate cut would increase," Ong added.

The 10-year bond futures contract had raced to its highest level since February at 92.250 before the data, some 50 basis points from its low at the beginning of the month, and had taken the cash yield to around 7.75 percent.
June bill futures had also firmed, touching a pre-data peak of 94.17. At its eventual 94.06 close, it equated to a cash rate of 5.94 percent compared with current 6.0 percent official interest rates.

The local market's retracement from its early highs saw spreads reverse their initial tightening to the U.S. U.S. yields had eased on Tuesday following a solid response to a two-year note sale and on hopes of a balanced budget agreement soon. A US$12.5 billion 5-year note sale is due later today.
